feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iterations 0, 1 and 2 gave identical race metrics to four decimals on all three tracks (score 26.0449, max_error 0.0609 to 0.0614 m, one line-loss event per trial, progress 0.035 to 0.115, no finishes). That holds across three different geometry changes: spread 0.02 to 0.03 m (iteration 1), footprint 12 to 16 mm (iteration 2), and the rescaled weights. The 0.06 m off-track floor is the binding limit, not the body term (0.0425 m at body_width 0.12). Because geometry changes have not moved the outcome, the first check is whether the race data is repeating. If the iteration-3 race matches iterations 0 to 2 again, stop geometry changes and check the pipeline. If the metrics differ, the wheel_track change is the cause, and the next step depends on what it shows. Rule (a): if max_error falls below 0.06 m and line_loss_events reach zero, keep wheel_track 0.10 m and change nothing else for one race. Rule (b): if line_loss_events stay at one or more with max_error near 0.06 m, go to wheel_track 0.08 m (the minimum), since yaw response is still the limit. Rule (c): if steering_oscillation rises sharply on the slalom while line loss is zero, the narrower track is over-steering, so try wheel_track 0.11 m as the midpoint with the same sensors.
requested_changes: Keep wheel_track at 0.10 m with the 16 mm footprint and the 0.03 m spread for one race. If the metrics match iterations 0 to 2 exactly, stop geometry changes and check the race data pipeline before any further test.

If line_loss_events stay at one or more and max_error stays near 0.06 m with different metrics, test wheel_track 0.08 m (the minimum), keeping all other geometry fixed, to test whether more yaw response closes the gap.
If steering_oscillation rises sharply on the slalom with zero line loss, test wheel_track 0.11 m to back off the yaw response, keeping the sensor geometry fixed.
